outcome.description: 'answered', 'absent' or 'error'. Three states, never two: absent is normal, error is a source that exists and could not be read, and merging them would hide a corrupt anchor file behind 'no anchor configured'.
outcome.title: Outcome

source_detail.description: Which one — a path, or free text.

AnchorCadenceModel.description:
How often this boot anchored its head.

The widest gap is the useful figure: it is how long the chain went
without an external witness, and therefore how wide an "existed by"
bracket would be for records inside it.

count.description: Anchor records written during this boot.
count.title: Count

widest_gap_ns.description: Longest interval between anchors, in nanoseconds.

AnchorProfile.description:
An ordered list of places to look for a trusted head.

Order is meaningful and is the user's: the first source that answers wins,
and the ones before it are reported as tried. That is why resolution is
availability-first — a source that errors does not stop the walk — and why
the provenance view has to show what was skipped rather than only what
answered.

name.description: Profile name, used as the verify parameter.
name.title: Name

sources.description: Tried in order; the first that answers is used.
sources.title: Sources

AnchorReadingModel.description: The head that answered, and where it came from.

head.description: The hex head this check was made against.
head.title: Head

AnchorReadingModel.title: AnchorReadingModel

AnchorSourceSpec.description:
One place a trusted head might live.

The shell owns the concrete sources; the package owns what a head means
(L2). A spec is therefore plain data — no package type appears in a
request model.

account.description: For kind='keychain': the account name the head is stored under. The service name is fixed by the application, so this is the only part an operator chooses.
account.title: Account

detail.description: Free text shown beside this source in the provenance view.
detail.title: Detail

head.description: For kind='manual': the 64-character hex head, as handed over.
head.title: Head

path.description: For kind='file': path to a FileAnchor head file.
path.title: Path

AnchorSourceSpec.title: AnchorSourceSpec

BootBoundary.description:
Where one boot begins and ends, on both axes.

Rendered as an axis break rather than a seam (§C-03). `monotonic_ns`
resets across a boot, so no duration spans one — and nothing in this
payload computes one that does.

first_wall_ns.description: Wall clock at its first record.
first_wall_ns.title: First Wall Ns

last_wall_ns.description: Wall clock at its last record.
last_wall_ns.title: Last Wall Ns

BootBoundary.title: BootBoundary

BootView.description:
One boot, with the statistics the package computes for it.

A boot is the unit that matters for reading time: `monotonic_ns` resets
across a boundary, so no duration spans one.

recovery_seq.description: Where this boot recovered a truncated tail, when it did. Null is the ordinary case rather than a missing value.
recovery_seq.title: Recovery Seq

time_trust_values.description: Every wall-clock trust level seen inside this boot. More than one means the clock changed status mid-boot, which qualifies every wall-time claim in it — so the set is carried rather than reduced to the latest.
time_trust_values.title: Time Trust Values

uptime_ns.description: Monotonic span of this boot, computed by the package.
uptime_ns.title: Uptime Ns

BootView.title: BootView

ChainResult.description:
Question one, first half: do these records link to each other?

Always answerable. It needs no key and no anchor — only the bytes in
front of it — which is why it is the one question a chain can never
decline to answer.

**It is a header walk.** Whether each record still *is* the bytes its
header claims is a separate question, answered by
:class:`ContainerCheck`. A consumer that renders `chain_ok` alone will
show a sound file when a body has been swapped.

breaks.description: Sequence numbers where prev_hash does not name the predecessor.
breaks.title: Breaks

chain_ok.description: Whether every record header links to its predecessor. Headers only — see ContainerCheck.body_digest_mismatches for whether the bodies still match their digests.
chain_ok.title: Chain Ok

gaps.description: Skipped sequence numbers. A gap is a break whether or not the hashes on either side happen to link.
gaps.title: Gaps

head.description: Hex digest of the last record in the chain.
head.title: Head

uninterpretable.description: Records with an unknown format version or record type. Chain-checked and reported, never rejected — the verifier not understanding a record is not the same as the record being wrong.
uninterpretable.title: Uninterpretable

violations.description: (seq, reason) pairs for normative MUSTs the record broke. Kept as pairs: a seq without its reason is a number nobody can act on.
violations.title: Violations

ChainResult.title: ChainResult

ChainSubject.description:
What the container *is*, stated before any verdict about it.

Separate from the verification result on purpose: a reader of a report
must be able to confirm they are holding the same artifact the check ran
against, independently of whether that check passed.

assurance_tiers.description: Every assurance tier the chain's records carry, not just the latest. More than one means the platform guarantee changed mid-chain, and the verdict wording cannot then be a single sentence — so the set is reported rather than reduced.
assurance_tiers.title: Assurance Tiers

bytes.description: File size on disk, in bytes.
bytes.title: Bytes

filename.description: The file's name, for display only.
filename.title: Filename

records.description: Number of records the reader found.
records.title: Records

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the file as opened. Identifies the artifact; a report naming only a filename identifies nothing.
sha256.title: Sha256

time_trust_values.description: Every wall-clock trust level the chain's records carry. More than one means the writer's clock changed status mid-chain, which qualifies every wall-time claim in the file.
time_trust_values.title: Time Trust Values

ChainSubject.title: ChainSubject

Completeness.description:
Question two: is what I hold all of it?

The only question that can go unasked, and the answer must say so.

anchor_lag.description: Records present beyond the anchored head, when there are any.
anchor_lag.title: Anchor Lag

anchor_reason.description: The verifier's sentence explaining an incomplete answer.
anchor_reason.title: Anchor Reason

complete_to_anchor.description: True, False, or null. Null means NO ANCHOR ANSWERED — either none was configured, or every source in the profile was absent — so the question was never asked. It is not a pass and must never be rendered as one.
complete_to_anchor.title: Complete To Anchor

Completeness.title: Completeness

ContainerCheck.description:
Whether each record is the bytes its own header claims.

A different question from the one `ChainResult` answers. The chain is
about how records link to each other; this is about whether a record's
body still hashes to the `body_digest` its header carries.

`AuditReader.verify()` does not perform this comparison — that is by
design, and it is why verification needs no keys. The walk comes from the
package's report builder, so the shell never decides what a body digest
means.

body_digest_mismatches.description: Sequence numbers whose body does not hash to the digest their header carries. NON-EMPTY MEANS THE HEADER CHAIN CAN STILL BE INTACT — a swapped body leaves every link verifying, so a consumer that renders chain_ok alone would show a sound file. The answer to 'is what I hold internally consistent?' requires this list to be empty as well.
body_digest_mismatches.title: Body Digest Mismatches

malformed.description: The parser's sentence, when it could not finish.
malformed.title: Malformed

well_formed.description: Whether the container parsed end to end as PALA-1.
well_formed.title: Well Formed

ContainerCheck.title: ContainerCheck

DiagnosisModel.description:
What the failure looks like, rather than that there was one.

The pattern is the machine-readable part and a consumer may key visuals
off it. The narrative is the package's own sentence, carried verbatim:
a shell may show a localised sentence beside it, never instead of it, or
the report stops saying what the verifier said.

at_seq.description: Where, when the pattern has a location.
at_seq.title: At Seq

expected.description: What the verifier expected to find.
expected.title: Expected

pattern.description: One of: truncated_tail, prefix_absent, seq_gap, chain_break, record_violation, unanchored_tail, replaced_or_rolled_back.
pattern.title: Pattern

DiagnosisModel.title: DiagnosisModel

HealthResponse.description:
Liveness, and the identity of the verifier behind this service.

The verifier identity is part of the liveness answer rather than a
separate endpoint because a verification result is only meaningful
alongside the verifier that produced it. A shell that knows the service is
up but not what it is linked against knows less than it needs.

authenticated.description: Whether the session token gate is enforced. False means the sidecar was started without a token and any local process can reach it — a development affordance, never a supported configuration.
authenticated.title: Authenticated

package.description: The verifier package and version, e.g. 'palimpsests 0.8.0'.
package.title: Package

spec.description: The wire format the linked verifier implements, e.g. 'PALA-1 format_version 1'.
spec.title: Spec

HealthResponse.title: HealthResponse

KeychainSeedRequest.description: Store a head in the secret store under an account name.

account.description: Account name to store it under.
account.title: Account

KeychainSeedRequest.title: KeychainSeedRequest

KeychainStatus.description: Whether this machine has a usable secret store at all.

available.description: False means there is nowhere on this machine to keep an anchor — a headless box with no Secret Service, a session without credentials, or the keyring extra not installed. Distinct from 'your anchor was not found', and a UI that conflates the two sends the operator to look for a value that could never have been read.
available.title: Available

detail.description: What to do about it, when there is something to do.
detail.title: Detail

KeychainStatus.title: KeychainStatus

NamedValue.description:
A header enum value, with the package's name for it.

Both halves travel. The name is what a person reads; the number is what
survives a name table changing and what can be checked against the
specification. `name` is null when this verifier build has no name for
the value — which is a real answer, and better than a label invented to
fill the gap.

name.description: The package's name, or null if this build does not know it.
name.title: Name

NamedValue.title: NamedValue

OriginModel.description:
What was running when a record was written.

Every field is a **Recorded** claim: the writer declared it, and nothing
in the chain proves the process was actually running that model. The
digests let a reader compare against an artifact they hold; they do not
establish what produced the records.

config_digest.description: Hex digest of the configuration as the writer declared it.
config_digest.title: Config Digest

detail.description: Free text the writer attached, when it attached any.
detail.title: Detail

model_digest.description: Hex digest of the model as the writer declared it.
model_digest.title: Model Digest

since_seq.description: The record that declared this origin. A reader can jump to it and see the declaration rather than take this on trust — the same reason every other claim here names its source.
since_seq.title: Since Seq

OriginModel.title: OriginModel

RecordPage.description:
A window onto the records.

Paginated because a chain has no bound: a container from a busy
deployment can hold millions of records, and an endpoint that serialised
all of them would fail in the situation where the tool is most needed.

has_more.description: Whether records remain past this window. Stated rather than left to be inferred from len(records) == limit, which is ambiguous when a window ends exactly on the last record.
has_more.title: Has More

limit.description: Most records this window would return.
limit.title: Limit

offset.description: First sequence number this window could include.
offset.title: Offset

total.description: Records that MATCHED THE FILTERS, not records in the file. With no filters the two are the same, which is why this field could quietly say the wrong thing once filters existed: a total counting everything would print '3 of 40000' above three rows that are the only three there are.
total.title: Total

RecordPage.title: RecordPage

RecordView.description:
One record, as structure rather than as content.

Header fields and the shape of the body. What is *inside* a record is a
separate view with its own decisions about keys and redaction.

body_tlv_types.description: TLV types present in the body, or null when this view has none to show — a record type with no body, an encrypted body, or one this build cannot parse. Distinct from [], which would mean a decoded body containing nothing.
body_tlv_types.title: Body Tlv Types

key_id.description: Encryption key identifier, or null when the body is not encrypted.
key_id.title: Key Id

kind.description: Raw kind, for types that carry one.
kind.title: Kind

kind_name.description: The package's name for the kind. Null where the record type has no kind at all — GENESIS, BOOT and ANCHOR do not — which is not the same as a kind this build cannot name.
kind_name.title: Kind Name

monotonic_ns.description: Monotonic clock. Comparable only within one boot.
monotonic_ns.title: Monotonic Ns

parent_span_id.description: The enclosing span, when there is one.
parent_span_id.title: Parent Span Id

span_id.description: Hex span identifier, or null when the record is in no span. PALA-1 spells that as sixteen zero bytes; this field reports null rather than a span named 00000000…
span_id.title: Span Id

type_name.description: The package's name for the type, or null if unknown to this build.
type_name.title: Type Name

wall_clock_ns.description: The writer's wall clock. A Recorded claim, qualified by time_trust.
wall_clock_ns.title: Wall Clock Ns

RecordView.title: RecordView

SessionResponse.description: A session over one open container.

verifier.description: The verifier package and wire format behind this session. Carried on the session rather than fetched separately, because a result is only meaningful alongside the verifier that produced it.
verifier.title: Verifier

SessionResponse.title: SessionResponse

SpanStatsModel.description: Spans opened during this boot, and how many were left open.

closed.description: Spans that have an end record.
closed.title: Closed

median_duration_ns.description: Median closed-span duration, or null when none closed.
median_duration_ns.title: Median Duration Ns

open.description: Spans opened and never closed. Evidence of an interrupted operation, not a defect in the log.
open.title: Open

open_rate.description: Open spans as a fraction, or null when there were no spans.
open_rate.title: Open Rate

SpanStatsModel.title: SpanStatsModel

SpanView.description: One span, and the records it covers.

end_seq.description: The SPAN_END record, or NULL FOR A SPAN NEVER CLOSED. Null is first-class evidence — an interrupted operation looks exactly like this — and must never be filled in with the last record seen.
end_seq.title: End Seq

parent_span_id.description: The enclosing span, or null at the top level.
parent_span_id.title: Parent Span Id

start_seq.description: The SPAN_START record, or null when it is not in this file.
start_seq.title: Start Seq

SpanView.title: SpanView

TimeStepModel.description: A step in the writer's clock, as the package detected it.

kind.description: The package's name for the kind of step.
kind.title: Kind

TimeStepModel.title: TimeStepModel

Timeline.description:
Record density along one axis, and what breaks the ruler.

**Two axes, and they are not interchangeable (L3).** `seq` is proved
order: the hash chain establishes it and nothing can reorder it. `wall`
is the writer's clock — a recorded claim, qualified by `time_trust`.

align.description: Null for uniform buckets, 'day' when each bucket is one UTC calendar day. A CONSUMER RENDERING DATES MUST CHECK THIS: a date printed from a uniform bucket's start is a date the records inside it may not have happened on, because such a bucket straddles midnight.
align.title: Align

basis.description: 'proved' for the seq axis, 'recorded' for the wall axis. Carried as its own field rather than left to be derived from `axis`, so a consumer cannot label a wall chart 'proved' by reading the wrong one.
basis.title: Basis

boot_boundaries.description: Reported apart from the series, because they are axis breaks.
boot_boundaries.title: Boot Boundaries

buckets.description: Equal-width intervals covering the range, empty ones included. How many there are depends on `align`: without it the range is divided into at most the number requested; with 'day' each is one calendar day and the count is however many days the chain spans.
buckets.title: Buckets

start.description: Where the first bucket begins. Equal to the lowest position on this axis for uniform buckets, and THE UTC MIDNIGHT AT OR BEFORE IT when align='day' — the first day is a whole day even when the chain starts in the middle of one.
start.title: Start

steps.description: Clock steps the package detected, with where and how far.
steps.title: Steps

time_trust_values.description: Every clock-trust level the records carry. The watermark for a wall-time view: it says whose clock this is, and how much the writer claimed for it.
time_trust_values.title: Time Trust Values

wall_follows_seq.description: Whether wall_clock_ns is non-decreasing along proved order. FALSE MEANS THE WALL AXIS REORDERS RECORDS relative to the chain, and a UI showing that axis must say so.
wall_follows_seq.title: Wall Follows Seq

wall_gaps.description: The intervals between boots, where the ruler does not apply.
wall_gaps.title: Wall Gaps

Timeline.title: Timeline

TimelineBucket.description:
One interval of the axis, and what fell inside it.

Present even when empty. An empty stretch is a fact about the chain —
the quiet week, the gap between boots — and a series that omitted empty
buckets would draw a dense chain out of a sparse one.

anchor.description: How many of them are ANCHOR records.
anchor.title: Anchor

end.description: Last position in this bucket, inclusive.
end.title: End

safety.description: How many of them are SAFETY records.
safety.title: Safety

start.description: First position in this bucket, inclusive.
start.title: Start

stepped.description: Whether the writer's clock stepped inside this bucket. On the wall axis a stepped bucket is measuring two different clocks, so its width means nothing — a UI must mark it rather than draw it like the others.
stepped.title: Stepped

TimelineBucket.title: TimelineBucket

VerificationResponse.description:
The verifier's answer, passed through rather than summarised.

There is deliberately no single "valid" field. The three questions have
three separate answers, one of which can be "not asked", and any field
that collapsed them would be the shell deciding what a verdict means.

anchor.description: The source that answered, or null when none did. A completeness answer is worth exactly as much as the anchor behind it, so the two are never separated.

anchor_attempts.description: Every source consulted, in order, including those that were absent or failed. The answering source alone would let a UI present it as 'the' anchor while silently skipping a source the operator believed was authoritative.
anchor_attempts.title: Anchor Attempts

container.description: The body-digest walk. Required rather than optional: a response that could omit it would let a consumer answer question one from the header chain alone.

session_id.description: The session this answer is about.
session_id.title: Session Id

subject_sha256.description: Digest of the file this answer describes. Repeated here so a verification result cannot be separated from its subject.
subject_sha256.title: Subject Sha256

verifier.description: Package and wire format behind it.
verifier.title: Verifier

VerificationResponse.title: VerificationResponse

WallGap.description:
The wall-clock distance between one boot's end and the next one's start.

Reported with both ends so a consumer can hatch the interval and **remove
the ruler inside it**: the clock is unverifiable while the system is
down, which is a statement about the gap rather than about the records
on either side.

duration_ns.description: to_wall_ns minus from_wall_ns. CAN BE NEGATIVE — that means the writer's clock moved backwards across the boundary, which the ruler cannot represent and a UI must not hide.
duration_ns.title: Duration Ns

from_wall_ns.description: Wall clock at the earlier boot's last record.
from_wall_ns.title: From Wall Ns

to_wall_ns.description: Wall clock at the later boot's first record.
to_wall_ns.title: To Wall Ns

WallGap.title: WallGap

get.description:
Whether this machine can keep an anchor at all.

Asked before the operator configures a keychain profile, so the UI
can say "this machine has nowhere to keep one" rather than letting
them configure a source that will report absent forever.

put.description:
Store a head in the secret store.

This writes, and the read-only rule still holds: the target is
Auditor's own anchor store, never an audited container. The rule is
about not touching evidence, not about never writing a byte.

It exists so an operator can seed an anchor from the application
rather than from a shell one-liner they have to get exactly right —
and a head seeded with a typo persists, so getting it right matters
more here than anywhere else.

get.description: Every profile this sidecar knows, including the empty one.

schema.title: Response List Profiles Anchors Profiles Get

put.description:
Define or replace a profile.

The body's `name` is ignored in favour of the path, so a profile
cannot be defined under one name and answer to another.

get.description:
Liveness probe, and the identity triple the UI displays.

The verifier version is reported because a verification result is only
meaningful alongside the verifier that produced it.

post.description:
Open a container and return what it is.

Deliberately says nothing about whether the chain verifies. Identity
and structure are established first, and separately: a reader of a
report must be able to confirm they hold the same artifact the check
ran against, whether or not that check passed.

get.description:
The boots in this container, with their statistics.

Browsing is separate from verifying, and answers no question about
soundness. A chain that fails verification is still browsed — half
the job is inspecting evidence that did not pass.

schema.title: Response Session Boots Session  Session Id  Boots Get

get.description:
What was running when a record was written, or null if unstated.

**Null is an answer, not an absence.** Nothing before the first
MODEL_LOAD has an origin, because none had been declared — and a UI
must render that as "not stated in this file" rather than as an
empty card, which would read as "nothing was running".

200 with a null body rather than 404 for that reason: the question
was answered, and the answer is that the file does not say.

parameters.description: The record to ask about. Required rather than defaulted: origin changes along a chain, so an unasked-for default would answer a different question than the caller meant.

One record by sequence number.

404 when the file holds no such record. A segment covering records
400–900 legitimately has no record 12, and saying so is different
from saying the session is unknown — which the caller can tell apart
because that 404 names the session instead.

A window onto the records, as structure rather than content.

`total` counts the records that matched the filters, not the records
in the file. A total that counted everything would print "3 of 40000"
above three rows that are the only three there are.

get.description:
The verifier's answer about this session's container.

Re-checks the file digest first. A verdict about bytes that have since
changed is worse than no verdict, because it looks like one.

Note what this endpoint does NOT return: a single "valid" field. The
three questions have three separate answers, one of which can be "not
asked", and collapsing them here would be the shell deciding what a
verdict means — which is the one thing ADR-0001 exists to prevent.
